key_insight: A semi-analytical inverse design framework uses geometric frustration and instability to program anisotropic kirigami sheets into bistable, directionally deployable 3D shapes.
engineering_relevance: This enables rigid-material morphing structures with tunable stable states for soft robotics, biomedical devices, adaptive architecture, and aerospace applications.
method: Build a semi-analytical mechanical model linked to geometry and the energy landscape.
Use inverse design to encode anisotropy and bistability via controlled geometric frustration.
Validate predicted morphing behavior with finite element simulations and experiments.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement between model predictions, finite element simulations, and physical experiments showing stable deployed configurations and programmable anisotropic morphing.
watch_item: Practical deployment will depend on precise fabrication and sensitivity to geometric tolerances, which may affect bistability and repeatability.
